GET /api/health.notes: Retain as the Railway liveness/readiness protocol. It must remain cheap, unauthenticated, and independent of GraphQL execution. NestJS now serves its own structural equivalent (OperationalStatusController) at the same path. Deliberately NOT proxied: a health probe must describe the process that answers it, so each runtime reports itself; the Nest response mirrors the retained shape (status/checks/optional configuration) for monitors and becomes authoritative at direct-origin cutover.

GET /api/invoices/:id/pdf.notes: NestJS owns the retained cookie-authenticated binary route with selected-organization concealment, the legacy renderer's tenant snapshot, validated PDF output, safe attachment naming, and private/no-store, nosniff, sandbox headers. The existing origin proxies this exact URL behind a default-off server flag; the active frontend controls download the blob without selecting a transport.

POST /api/invoices/businesses/:id/logo.notes: NestJS retains tenant-authorized multipart HTTP with a 2 MiB limit, bounded parts, structural PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP checks, server-owned names, store-first replacement, durable old-logo cleanup, and compensating cleanup on database failure. A default-off legacy-origin proxy preserves rollback.

POST /api/invoices/settings/logo.notes: NestJS retains tenant-authorized multipart HTTP with a 2 MiB limit, bounded parts, structural PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP checks, server-owned names, store-first replacement, durable old-logo cleanup, and compensating cleanup on database failure. A default-off legacy-origin proxy preserves rollback.

POST /api/invoices/webhook/stripe.notes: NestJS retains the signed webhook over HTTP, verifies the exact raw bytes with Stripe's SDK, fails closed without its secret, and commits the event claim, payment, PostgreSQL balance update, and one paid-workflow trigger transactionally. A default-off legacy-origin proxy preserves rollback.

POST /api/billing/webhook.notes: Retain the exact raw-body Stripe signature protocol. The callback claims event IDs transactionally, locks tenant mappings, persists minimal replay snapshots, and atomically updates organization/subscription/audit state. Provider time plus event ID gives deterministic same-second ordering. Leased workers reconcile unmatched/ambiguous mappings and deliver upgrade notifications with retry, provider idempotency, and redacted dead letters. Operator dashboards and manual dead-letter controls remain platform work. NestJS now owns an identical implementation (SubscriptionWebhooksModule) verifying the exact signed bytes with the Stripe SDK and faithfully porting the durable event claim with minimal replay snapshot, deterministic provider ordering, tenant locks, plan/limit application, subscription upsert, audit trail, terminal transitions, and unmatched/ambiguous quarantine, proven by a dual-runtime PostgreSQL parity suite with genuinely signed payloads and cross-runtime deduplication; the legacy origin routes the path through a default-off proxy (SUBSCRIPTION_WEBHOOKS_NESTJS_ENABLED) forwarding the raw bytes and signature. The legacy reconciliation and notification workers keep draining the shared tables until the scheduler moves.

POST /api/webhooks/:workflowId.notes: Retain raw-body HMAC HTTP delivery with timestamp tolerance, canonical trigger matching, and durable replay claims. The adapter returns execution=durably_queued and feeds the same leased trigger matcher as first-party producers. NestJS now owns an identical implementation (WorkflowWebhooksModule) mirroring the raw-body HMAC verification with timestamp tolerance, canonical trigger normalization, and the durable delivery-key/event-key replay claim, proven by a dual-runtime PostgreSQL parity suite with genuinely signed payloads and cross-runtime replay deduplication; the legacy origin routes the path through a default-off proxy (WORKFLOW_WEBHOOKS_NESTJS_ENABLED) forwarding the exact raw bytes and signature headers. The port also repaired the retained validation middleware, whose 400 details had broken under the zod v4 upgrade (ZodError.errors removed) and returned an HTML error page instead of the documented JSON.

POST /api/email/webhook/resend.notes: Retain raw-body Svix verification and fail closed without the signing secret. Durable svix-id claims deduplicate delivery, provider occurrence timestamps prevent status regression, and matched logs/campaign recipients update engagement and contact suppression. Unmatched or cross-tenant ambiguous events are leased and retried from bounded claim fields until exactly one organization mapping exists; exhausted attempts become redacted dead letters. NestJS now owns an identical implementation (EmailWebhooksModule) with the same Resend SDK signature verification over the captured raw bytes and a faithful port of the durable svix-id claim, status-regression, suppression, and quarantine semantics, proven by a dual-runtime PostgreSQL parity suite using genuinely signed payloads (including cross-runtime deduplication through the shared claim table); the legacy origin routes the path through a default-off proxy (EMAIL_WEBHOOKS_NESTJS_ENABLED) that forwards the exact raw bytes and svix headers and falls through to the retained handler. The legacy reconciliation worker continues to drain the shared email_webhook_events table until the scheduler moves.

POST /api/sms-templates/webhook/inbound.notes: Retain Twilio-signed form HTTP, fail closed in production, and claim MessageSid durably. The globally unique normalized To number selects one owning organization before From is matched only among that tenant's contacts; unmatched receivers and ambiguous or missing tenant-local senders are quarantined without attribution. NestJS now owns an identical implementation (SmsWebhooksModule) mirroring the Twilio form-signature decision table over the public URL, the durable event-key claim, the provider-to-domain status map, receiving-number routing, tenant-local sender matching, and quarantine reasons, proven by a dual-runtime PostgreSQL parity suite including cross-runtime claim deduplication; the legacy origin routes both paths through a default-off proxy (SMS_WEBHOOKS_NESTJS_ENABLED) that forwards the raw form bytes, the Twilio signature, and the original protocol/host so URL-bound validation still succeeds upstream.

POST /api/sms-templates/webhook/status.notes: Retain Twilio-signed form HTTP with durable MessageSid/status claims and an explicit provider-to-domain status map. NestJS now owns an identical implementation (SmsWebhooksModule) mirroring the Twilio form-signature decision table over the public URL, the durable event-key claim, the provider-to-domain status map, receiving-number routing, tenant-local sender matching, and quarantine reasons, proven by a dual-runtime PostgreSQL parity suite including cross-runtime claim deduplication; the legacy origin routes both paths through a default-off proxy (SMS_WEBHOOKS_NESTJS_ENABLED) that forwards the raw form bytes, the Twilio signature, and the original protocol/host so URL-bound validation still succeeds upstream.

GET /api/contacts/export/csv.notes: Retain authenticated CSV HTTP with organization filters, private/no-store delivery, RFC-style quoting, spreadsheet-formula neutralization, and a 50,000-row rejection boundary.

POST /api/contacts/import/csv.notes: Despite the legacy path, this accepts JSON contact rows rather than multipart CSV. Retain HTTP during cutover with an exact object envelope, strict boolean duplicate policy, a 10,000-row limit, bounded 500-row inserts, and serialized plan-limit enforcement.

GET /api/forms/public/form/:identifier.notes: Retained anonymous rate-limited HTTP for embeds uses the global public identifier, with ambiguous legacy slugs failing closed. NestJS now owns an identical implementation (PublicFormsModule, including a faithful port of the public-form validation contract) proven by a dual-runtime PostgreSQL parity suite covering the validation matrix, conditional requirements, contact reuse, and durable trigger/notification fan-out; the legacy origin routes this path through a default-off proxy (PUBLIC_FORMS_NESTJS_ENABLED) that falls through to the retained handler and replicates the dedicated submission rate limit on the proxied path.

POST /api/forms/public/form/:identifier.notes: Retained anonymous rate-limited HTTP commits contact reuse and submission transactionally with same-email serialization, complete field validation, and durable notification/event delivery. NestJS now owns an identical implementation (PublicFormsModule, including a faithful port of the public-form validation contract) proven by a dual-runtime PostgreSQL parity suite covering the validation matrix, conditional requirements, contact reuse, and durable trigger/notification fan-out; the legacy origin routes this path through a default-off proxy (PUBLIC_FORMS_NESTJS_ENABLED) that falls through to the retained handler and replicates the dedicated submission rate limit on the proxied path.

GET /api/bookings/public/book/:slug.notes: Anonymous rate-limited embed protocol resolves a globally unique cal_ public ID first and retains slug compatibility only when exactly one active calendar matches. Authenticated REST/GraphQL projections and the calendar link UI expose the stable public ID. NestJS now owns an identical implementation (PublicBookingsModule) proven by a dual-runtime PostgreSQL parity suite; the legacy origin routes this path through a default-off proxy (PUBLIC_BOOKINGS_NESTJS_ENABLED) that preserves legacy rollback by falling through to the retained handler.

GET /api/bookings/public/book/:slug/slot.notes: Resolves the global public ID with an exactly-one-match legacy slug fallback and returns only concrete timezone-aware slots for a bounded 31-day range. Generation and every booking write share one PostgreSQL policy for effective windows, overrides, activity, duration, buffers, notice, horizon, DST, booking collisions, and normalized external busy intervals. NestJS now owns an identical implementation (PublicBookingsModule) proven by a dual-runtime PostgreSQL parity suite; the legacy origin routes this path through a default-off proxy (PUBLIC_BOOKINGS_NESTJS_ENABLED) that preserves legacy rollback by falling through to the retained handler.

POST /api/bookings/public/book/:slug.notes: Anonymous rate-limited booking resolves the global public ID, transactionally rechecks the shared authoritative slot policy after the calendar lock, serializes case-insensitive contact reuse, returns a 256-bit cancellation capability once, and stores only its SHA-256 hash with end-plus-one-day expiry. NestJS now owns an identical implementation (PublicBookingsModule) proven by a dual-runtime PostgreSQL parity suite; the legacy origin routes this path through a default-off proxy (PUBLIC_BOOKINGS_NESTJS_ENABLED) that preserves legacy rollback by falling through to the retained handler.

POST /api/bookings/public/book/:slug/can.notes: Hashes the supplied 256-bit capability, binds it to the resolved calendar and confirmed booking, requires unexpired end-plus-one-day capability state, and clears hash/expiry on success. Malformed, wrong-calendar, expired, and replay attempts share a non-enumerating miss; raw tokens are forbidden in PostgreSQL and excluded from authenticated REST/GraphQL projections. NestJS now owns an identical implementation (PublicBookingsModule) proven by a dual-runtime PostgreSQL parity suite; the legacy origin routes this path through a default-off proxy (PUBLIC_BOOKINGS_NESTJS_ENABLED) that preserves legacy rollback by falling through to the retained handler.

GET /api/calendar-integrations/google/au.notes: Currently retained on HTTP by the integration adapter because it begins a browser/provider redirect protocol. It returns a provider URL with short-lived signed user, organization, nonce, and safe return-path state.

GET /api/calendar-integrations/google/ca.notes: Provider redirect protocol; verifies signed expiring state and current organization membership before token exchange, then stores access/refresh credentials only as versioned AES-256-GCM envelopes under the active rotation key.

Currently retained on HTTP because it performs live provider I/O. The boundary is user-and-organization scoped with PostgreSQL row-locked token refresh, active-key rewrap, encrypted winning-generation persistence, and redacted provider errors. Fresh PostgreSQL proves concurrent callers issue one provider refresh.

POST /api/signatures/documents/upload.notes: NestJS owns the unchanged authenticated URL behind a default-off upload proxy. Bounded multipart parsing, CSRF, tenant/draft preflight plus row-lock recheck, PDF magic validation, private unguessable storage, SHA-256 metadata, version-1 convergence, replacement cleanup, and failed-commit compensation are covered by PostgreSQL tests. Malware scanning and structural/page validation remain production cutover blockers.

GET /api/signatures/documents/:id/file.notes: NestJS owns the unchanged authenticated URL behind a default-off read proxy. Tenant lookup precedes an allowlisted local/S3 read; successful responses use private no-store/nosniff/sandbox headers and a safe inline filename without exposing a permanent storage URL.

GET /api/signatures/documents/:id/downlo.notes: NestJS owns the unchanged authenticated URL behind a default-off read proxy. A tenant-owned signed locator is required; delivery accepts only exact private local/S3 storage and returns an attachment with private no-store/nosniff/sandbox headers and a safe filename.

GET /api/signatures/templates/:id/file.notes: NestJS owns the unchanged authenticated URL behind a default-off read proxy. Tenant lookup precedes the exact private local/S3 allowlist; the response uses hardened headers and a safe inline filename.

POST /api/signatures/templates/upload.notes: NestJS owns the unchanged authenticated URL behind a default-off upload proxy. Bounded multipart parsing, CSRF, tenant preflight plus row-lock recheck, PDF magic validation, private unguessable storage, SHA-256 metadata, replacement cleanup, and failed-commit compensation are covered by PostgreSQL tests. Malware scanning and structural/page validation remain production cutover blockers.

GET /api/public/sign/:token.notes: Rate-limited hashed capability protocol; active unexpired recipient/document only, with minimal sanitized public data.

POST /api/public/sign/:token.notes: Atomic one-time capability claim, exact field allowlist and validation, immutable audit event, and durable completion work.

POST /api/public/sign/:token/decline.notes: Atomic active-recipient decline, bounded reason, token revocation, lifecycle transition, and durable notification intent.

POST /api/public/sign/:token/verify.notes: Currently returns 410. Legacy draft configuration now rejects email/SMS verification so unsupported assurance cannot be advertised.

GET /api/public/sign/:token/file.notes: Capability-authorized private PDF stream with no arbitrary URL proxying and no view-state mutation.

GET /api/public/sign/:token/download.notes: Active signing capabilities receive the source PDF as a private attachment; completed-artifact delivery remains a separate product/lifecycle decision.

GET /api/shared/list/:token.notes: Rate-limited non-enumerating capability read with recursive sanitization and no-store/noindex headers. NestJS now owns an identical implementation (PublicSharingModule) proven by a dual-runtime PostgreSQL parity suite; the legacy origin routes this path through a default-off proxy (PUBLIC_SHARING_NESTJS_ENABLED) that preserves legacy rollback by falling through to the retained handler.

GET /api/shared/note/:token.notes: Rate-limited non-enumerating capability read; executable markup is sanitized and the response cannot be cached or indexed. NestJS now owns an identical implementation (PublicSharingModule) proven by a dual-runtime PostgreSQL parity suite; the legacy origin routes this path through a default-off proxy (PUBLIC_SHARING_NESTJS_ENABLED) that preserves legacy rollback by falling through to the retained handler.

GET /api/shared/whiteboard/:token.notes: Rate-limited capability read with recursive sanitization; canvas node and external-resource schemas still need an exact allowlist. NestJS now owns an identical implementation (PublicSharingModule) proven by a dual-runtime PostgreSQL parity suite; the legacy origin routes this path through a default-off proxy (PUBLIC_SHARING_NESTJS_ENABLED) that preserves legacy rollback by falling through to the retained handler.

GET /api/shared/wireframe/:token.notes: Intentional public-link protocol boundary. The rate-limited non-enumerating capability read returns an allowlisted recursively sanitized projection with no-store/noindex/no-referrer headers; the shipped read-only viewer handles live updates, deletion, and durable revocation. NestJS now owns an identical implementation (PublicSharingModule) proven by a dual-runtime PostgreSQL parity suite; the legacy origin routes this path through a default-off proxy (PUBLIC_SHARING_NESTJS_ENABLED) that preserves legacy rollback by falling through to the retained handler.

GET /api/shared/vault/:token.notes: Intentional rate-limited no-store public-link boundary. It rejects malformed, unknown, revoked, and locked capabilities; returns an allowlisted decrypted projection; and fails the complete response closed on any item decryption error. Hash-at-rest and browser telemetry verification remain security hardening. NestJS now owns an identical implementation (PublicSharingModule) proven by a dual-runtime PostgreSQL parity suite; the legacy origin routes this path through a default-off proxy (PUBLIC_SHARING_NESTJS_ENABLED) that preserves legacy rollback by falling through to the retained handler.

GET /api/chat-widget/public/config/:widg.notes: Retain the rate-limited public embed bootstrap over HTTP. The widget key selects an allowlisted active configuration projection; authenticated management and provider capabilities are absent.

POST /api/chat-widget/public/session.notes: Retain public visitor session creation over HTTP. It validates the widget capability and allowed-domain policy, then issues the opaque session capability used by the browser embed.

GET /api/chat-widget/public/messages/:se.notes: Retain rate-limited visitor polling over the opaque session capability. The authenticated GraphQL schema never exposes that bearer token; live delivery remains on the established Socket.IO protocol.

POST /api/chat-widget/public/messages.notes: Retain rate-limited public visitor message submission over the session capability. Agent replies originate in CSRF-protected GraphQL and reach this visitor protocol through the durable realtime outbox.

POST /api/chat-widget/public/end-session.notes: Retain the public terminal session action over the visitor capability. It is part of the externally embedded widget protocol rather than the authenticated operator API.

POST /api/chat-widget/public/typing.notes: Retain ephemeral public typing signals over the visitor capability and Socket.IO. This realtime transport boundary is intentionally not modeled as a GraphQL mutation.

GET /api/social/connect/facebook.notes: Retain browser OAuth initiation over HTTP. The authenticated organization context is bound to a short-lived server-side state record before redirecting to Meta; the frontend uses this endpoint only for top-level navigation.

GET /api/social/callback/facebook.notes: Retain the provider callback and browser redirect over HTTP. Single-use state selects the organization and actor before token exchange and channel persistence; GraphQL never receives provider authorization codes or access tokens.

GET /api/social/webhook.notes: Retain the Meta challenge protocol, compare the verify token in constant time, use dedicated configuration, and fail closed when it is absent.

POST /api/social/webhook.notes: Retain exact-body X-Hub-Signature-256 verification and fail closed without the app secret. One normalized durable batch claim precedes bounded inline processing; leased workers drain overflow and reconcile unmatched or ambiguous page/account mappings only when exactly one active organization remains. Durable message IDs prevent replay, Facebook and Instagram identities route separately, and socket delivery occurs only after commit.

GET /api/reputation/public/widget/:widge.notes: Retain credential-free rate-limited HTTP for third-party embedding. Exact 128-bit keys, no-store revocation, active-only configuration, tenant isolation, bounded review selection, and hidden/flagged exclusion are required. NestJS now owns an identical implementation (PublicReputationModule) proven by a dual-runtime PostgreSQL parity suite; the legacy origin routes this path through a default-off proxy (PUBLIC_REPUTATION_NESTJS_ENABLED) that preserves legacy rollback by falling through to the retained handler. The credential-free Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * boundary is still emitted by the legacy origin's CORS delegate ahead of the proxy; the NestJS CORS options must add the widget wildcard before any direct-origin cutover.

GET /api/reputation/public/review/:token.notes: Retain anonymous no-store capability HTTP with an exact 256-bit token, expiry, and minimal token-free projection. NestJS now owns an identical implementation (PublicReputationModule) proven by a dual-runtime PostgreSQL parity suite; the legacy origin routes this path through a default-off proxy (PUBLIC_REPUTATION_NESTJS_ENABLED) that preserves legacy rollback by falling through to the retained handler.

POST /api/reputation/public/review/:toke.notes: Retain anonymous rate-limited capability HTTP; row locking makes submission one-time and rating, text, platform, and redirect behavior are validated server-side. NestJS now owns an identical implementation (PublicReputationModule) proven by a dual-runtime PostgreSQL parity suite; the legacy origin routes this path through a default-off proxy (PUBLIC_REPUTATION_NESTJS_ENABLED) that preserves legacy rollback by falling through to the retained handler.

GET /api/pages/public/page/:slug.notes: Retain anonymous page delivery over HTTP for browser navigation, password capability checks, expiry enforcement, cache policy, and public rendering. NestJS now owns an identical implementation (PublicLandingPagesModule) proven by a dual-runtime PostgreSQL parity suite; the legacy origin routes this path through a default-off proxy (PUBLIC_LANDING_PAGES_NESTJS_ENABLED) that preserves legacy rollback by falling through to the retained handler.

POST /api/pages/public/page/:slug/analyt.notes: Retain the anonymous rate-limited analytics beacon over HTTP; it validates the published page and records request-derived device and attribution evidence. NestJS now owns an identical implementation (PublicLandingPagesModule) proven by a dual-runtime PostgreSQL parity suite; the legacy origin routes this path through a default-off proxy (PUBLIC_LANDING_PAGES_NESTJS_ENABLED) that preserves legacy rollback by falling through to the retained handler.

GET /api/invoice-integrations/stripe/con.dispositionReason: OAuth begin endpoint; part of the retained provider-OAuth protocol trio with its callback.
GET /api/invoice-integrations/stripe/con.notes: Retain as the authenticated OAuth begin step, matching the calendar and social provider-connection precedent: it mints signed state bound to the user and organization and returns the provider authorization URL. Keeping begin and callback in one HTTP module keeps state signing, expiry, and return-path rules in one place.

GET /api/invoice-integrations/stripe/cal.notes: Retain the browser redirect callback over HTTP. It validates signed state, exchanges the code with Stripe, persists the connected account for the organization, and redirects back to the frontend return path with success or error markers; provider errors and invalid state must fail closed to the fallback path without persisting a connection.

POST /api/invoice-integrations/stripe/di.dispositionReason: Authenticated tenant-scoped state change with a JSON envelope; matches the calendar provider connection-management mutations.
POST /api/invoice-integrations/stripe/di.notes: Migrate to a GraphQL mutation following the calendar provider-connection management precedent: authenticated, organization-scoped removal of the Stripe connection with an idempotent already-disconnected outcome. The retained REST route stays as rollback until the frontend consumer passes the per-slice exit gate.

GET /api/public/estimates/:token.dispositionReason: Anonymous token-capability endpoint; part of the retained public-estimate protocol, matching public signing.
GET /api/public/estimates/:token.notes: Retain anonymous token-scoped estimate delivery over HTTP for recipient browsers, matching the public-signing precedent. NestJS owns the implementation; the legacy origin routes this path through the rate-limited public-estimate proxy.

POST /api/public/estimates/:token/accept.notes: Retain the anonymous token-capability accept action over HTTP. NestJS owns the implementation behind the legacy origin's rate-limited public-estimate proxy; terminal-state estimates must deny repeated transitions.

POST /api/public/estimates/:token/declin.notes: Retain the anonymous token-capability decline action over HTTP. NestJS owns the implementation behind the legacy origin's rate-limited public-estimate proxy; terminal-state estimates must deny repeated transitions.

GET /api/status.notes: Retain as the verbose operational status endpoint alongside the readiness probe. The NestJS implementation should keep the response cheap and unauthenticated, and must not leak configuration beyond the current environment, uptime, version, and coarse health booleans. NestJS now serves its own structural equivalent (OperationalStatusController) at the same path, including this runtime's route inventory for the status page. Deliberately NOT proxied for the same process-probe reason as /api/health.
